title: The 11 offensive positions
summary: Who the O's are and what each one does.

steps.text: The offense has 11 players. Five of them are the offensive line: the center in the middle, a guard on each side of him, and a tackle outside each guard. They are the biggest players, and their job is to block.
The quarterback takes the snap from the center. He is the leader. He hands the ball off, throws it, or runs with it. Every play starts in his hands.
The running back lines up behind the quarterback. He takes handoffs and runs with the ball. He can also catch short passes and help block.
Wide receivers line up out wide, near the sidelines. They are fast. They run routes and catch passes. Coaches often call them by letters: X, Z, and Y.

The tight end lines up right next to a tackle. He is half blocker and half receiver: big enough to block, quick enough to catch. That is 5 linemen, a quarterback, a running back, three receivers, and a tight end. Eleven.

quiz.explanation: The quarterback lines up behind the center and takes the snap.

quiz.prompt: How many offensive linemen are there?
quiz.explanation: Five: a center, two guards, and two tackles.
The tight end lines up right next to the tackle on the end of the line.

quiz.prompt: Which player takes handoffs and runs with the ball most often?
quiz.explanation: The running back lines up behind the quarterback for exactly that job.
Wide receivers line up out near the sidelines. X, Y, and Z are all receivers.
